title: The first paycheck
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday. The first check from Heceta: a week's worth, three days, eight-fifty. Wood cashes it at the drugstore because the bank closes at three. The dimes go back in the cigar box first. Then the rest.

panels.composition: A check, small, handwritten: the shop's name as blocks, an amount as a smudge, the OWNER's signature a clean line.

image.prompt: close on a small handwritten paycheck with a smudged amount and a clean signature, black and white, no words
image.notes: The amount: a smudge (the strip's rule for money).

panels.composition: The drugstore counter. The CLERK counting bills out. WOOD. BARNABY at the door.

image.prompt: a drugstore clerk counting bills onto a counter for a young man while a small dog waits at the door, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The bedroom. The cigar box. Dimes going in first, a roll of them. Then the bills, folded, on top.

image.prompt: close on a cigar box in a desk drawer receiving a roll of dimes and then folded bills, black and white, no words

panels.composition: WOOD closing the drawer. The corkboard above: the PNCA letter over the bus schedule. The box under it has money in it now, for copies. That's the whole plan.

image.prompt: a young man closing a desk drawer beneath a corkboard pinned with an official letter over a bus schedule, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The first check. Dimes first. That's the whole plan.
